evidence.title: Incident Report: CRSB Reviewer Death
evidence.content: Dr. Petra Lindgren, a reviewer at the Continuity & Relief Standards Board, died hours before she was due to flag a Corvid protocol — internally named LOOM — for an ethics review. Ruled an accident.

evidence.title: Lindgren's Unsent Ethics-Review Draft
evidence.content:
DRAFT — NOT FILED

"LOOM does not merely gather disaster-response data. It issues recommendations predicting which small failures — thefts, leaks, sabotages — most effectively move a market or policy outcome. This is not risk analysis. This is a menu."

evidence.title: Building Access Log — Night of Death
evidence.content: Lindgren's badge logged an exit from the CRSB building. See Timeline for the exact sequence against her phone's final message.

evidence.title: Device-Wipe Utility — Recovered at Scene
evidence.content: Forensic recovery of a utility found on-site, used to wipe Lindgren's personal device after her death. Hash Compare returns a second confirmed hit against the same toolkit family first logged in Case 001, matched again in Case 005.

chat.text: They killed someone to protect a recommendation engine's output. This isn't about hiding a crime anymore — it's about controlling what happens next. Every case we've closed might have been exactly that: what was scheduled to happen next.

cctv.name: CRSB Rear Corridor
cctv.normalText: REAR CORRIDOR — routine, empty at this hour.
cctv.clueText:
[STAGED SCENE]

No third party visible in the corridor during the badge-exit window. Whatever happened, it wasn't a struggle anyone on this camera witnessed — the scene was arranged after the fact, not during it.

network.name: Vault_Secure_Node
network.desc: Location of the wiped personal device, recovered post-mortem.

TK-5F3C9A.payload: Same encryption/wipe toolkit family. Second confirmed hit, this time on a device-wipe utility found at a death scene.

timeline.title: Lindgren's Last Message Sent
timeline.text: "Filing the LOOM ethics flag first thing tomorrow. Don't let me forget." — sent to a CRSB colleague.

timeline.title: Badge Exit Logged
timeline.text: Lindgren's building badge logs an exit — eleven minutes BEFORE her own phone sent its last message.

timeline.title: Rear Corridor, Empty
timeline.text: No third party visible during the relevant window.

archive.commentary: Requires the reviewer's own filed report — which Lindgren never got to submit.

suspects.name: Ashcroft Maritime Security
suspects.notes: Device-wipe utility at the scene matches the same toolkit family confirmed in Cases 001 and 005 — the campaign's second confirmed registry hit.

solution.successMessage: Eleven minutes. That's the whole case — a badge exit logged eleven minutes before a phone sent a message from inside a building its owner had already, on paper, left. Nobody stages a scene that carefully by accident. The wipe-utility hash closes it: same toolkit, same hands, two cases apart.

onDocument.c7_ev02: LOOM isn't just data collection. It's a menu of which disasters to schedule. Every case so far might be an order off that menu.

onFlag.HASH_MATCHED_2: Second hit on the same toolkit. Apapa, Busan, now Vienna. This isn't a pattern anymore — it's an inventory.

onBookmark.c7_ev02: Bookmarked. The word LOOM matters now. It didn't yesterday.

narrativeBeats.onSubmitSuccess: Submission proves murder and puts LOOM on the record by name for the first time. Renata doesn't say 'good work' this time.
